title:
INEQUALITIES,
(REPRESENTING INEQUALITIES ON A NUMBER LINE)
objective: LO: I can represent linear inequalities on a number line using open and closed circles.

content.text: On a number line, an open circle (○) means the value is NOT included (< or >). A closed circle (●) means the value IS included (≤ or ≥).
Strategy: Solve the inequality first, then draw the number line with the correct circle and arrow/line.

examples.expr: x > 3: open circle at 3, arrow right
x ≤ 5: closed circle at 5, arrow left
2 < x ≤ 6: open at 2, closed at 6, line between
x > 3 uses a closed circle at 3
x ≤ 5 means arrow pointing right from 5

key_idea.title: Key idea
key_idea.text: Open circle = not included (strict). Closed circle = included (or equal to). Arrow shows the direction of valid values.
key_idea.caption: Open = excluded, Closed = included

modelled_examples.label: Example 1 – simple inequality
modelled_examples.question: Represent x > 2 on a number line
steps: Draw a number line with 2 marked
Place an open circle at 2 (not included)
Draw an arrow pointing right from 2
modelled_examples.explanation: The open circle shows that 2 itself is not a solution.

modelled_examples.label: Example 2 – less than or equal
modelled_examples.question: Represent x ≤ 4 on a number line
steps: Draw a number line with 4 marked
Draw an arrow pointing left from 4
modelled_examples.explanation: The closed circle shows that 4 IS a solution.

modelled_examples.label: Example 3 – compound inequality
modelled_examples.question: Represent −1 < x ≤ 3 on a number line
steps: Mark −1 and 3 on the number line
Open circle at −1 (not included), closed at 3 (included)
Draw a solid line between them
modelled_examples.answer: Open at −1, closed at 3, line between
modelled_examples.explanation: No arrows needed for a compound inequality, just the connecting line.

modelled_examples.label: Example 4 – solving then representing
modelled_examples.question: Solve 2x + 1 > 7 and represent on a number line
steps: Open circle at 3, arrow pointing right
modelled_examples.answer: x > 3: open circle at 3, arrow right
modelled_examples.explanation: Solve the inequality first, then draw the representation.

problems.text: Solve 2(x − 3) < x + 1 and 3x + 2 ≥ 5 simultaneously. Represent the solution on a number line and list all integer solutions.

A number line shows a closed circle at −2 and an open circle at 4 with a line between. Write this as a double inequality. If we then apply the transformation y = 2x + 1, what inequality does y satisfy?
